options.text: The harness denies the edit, because the rule is in the prompt.
options.why: Tempting. A rule in the prompt is words the model reads. Nothing in this board checks the edit.

options.text: The edit goes through, because a rule in the prompt is only a line.
options.why: Right. The board has no check on the edit, so the model's reply decides what happens.

options.text: The model stops and asks the user first.
options.why: Tempting. That would need a check, and this board does not have one.

outcome: The edit went through and the run ended as done. The test check failed.
question: The project rules say never touch tests/, and that is the only place the rule lives. The model's reply edits the test anyway. What happens?

options.text: The user, because the user is talking now.
options.why: Tempting. Who is talking is not the test. The layer's place in the hierarchy decides.

options.text: The system prompt, because the instruction hierarchy puts the operator's standing instructions above one message.
options.why: Right. The hierarchy follows who wrote the layer, and the standing rules set the limits.
Wrong. Length does not decide which layer wins.

question: The system prompt says fix the code. A user message says edit the test. Which one wins, and why?

options.why: Tempting. It is too high: a slogan that gives no action to take.

options.text: Never edit a file under tests/; fix the code the test calls instead, and run pytest before you say done.
options.why: Right. It is specific enough to act on and general enough to hold for any test in that folder.

options.text: On line 42 of calc.py, change the 3 to a 4.
options.why: Tempting. It is too low: a lookup table that breaks as soon as the file changes.

question: Which instruction has the right altitude?

options.text: Allow the call, because nothing says to stop it.
options.why: Tempting. That fails open, and the rule can be broken by a malformed call.

options.text: Deny the call, because a check that cannot decide fails closed.
options.why: Right. A hook that cannot decide denies, so a broken check cannot let an edit through.

options.text: Ask the model to try again with a path.
options.why: Tempting. The model's retry is not a check, and the hook still has to decide.

question: A pre-tool hook cannot read the path of a call it is checking. What should it do?

options.text: A manual that lists every case the team has ever seen.
options.why: Tempting. A map points to where things are; a manual tries to hold every case.

options.text: A short file: where the tests live, the command that runs them, and the few rules that must hold, each with its reason.
options.why: Right. A map says where things live and how to check them.

options.text: One line: MUST follow every rule, always.
options.why: Tempting. A line like that has no altitude and no way to check it.

question: Which rules file is written as a map?

options.text: Nothing: prompt lines do not need review.
options.why: Tempting. A changed rule can change every run after it, so it needs the same review as code.

options.text: The line is versioned, reviewed, and a test shows the rule still holds.
options.why: Right. Prompt lines are treated as code: versioned, reviewed and tested.

options.text: The line is made longer, so it is safer.
options.why: Tempting. Longer instructions are not safer.

question: A rule line in the rules file changes, and nothing else does. What should happen before it goes live?
